about: British road numbers said the way UK drivers say them (loop B170, BI-151): M/A/B glued to 1-2 digits as a number (M twenty five, A forty), 3 digits route style (A three oh three), 4 digits digit by digit with 0 as 'oh' (B four oh oh nine); A1(M) is 'A one M'; J10 is 'junction ten' when a motorway is named. Only in road context (the/onto/on/via/join/take/along/leave/exit/off/follow before, or Toll/junction/motorway/-bound/(anti)clockwise after, or paired with a road ref); 'A1 sauce', 'A4 paper', 'vitamin B12', 'Seat A12', 'B2B', 'M&M' stay. Backseat Driver: backseat::pronunciation::ForSpeech / UkRoads (libs/backseat/pronunciation_uk_roads.hpp). Shared with BookLyre (CROSS).
